notes: curated: lt.json#tinta_higher_thres | euromod value in force at 2025-06-01: '100%*$MMS' from 2016-01-01 | value leg not scored: the selection states no expected_value (the law's value is not established for this case yet) | DERIVE — EUROMOD holds '100%*$MMS'. the income point at which the higher basic PIT allowance starts being withdrawn. GPMĮ art. 20(1) sets it by reference, not by amount: the maximum annual NPD applies while annual income does not exceed 'minimaliosios menesines algos, galiojusios einamuju kalendoriniu metu sausio 1 diena, dvylikos dydziu suma' — twelve times the minimum monthly wage in force on 1 January. EUROMOD stores the monthly form of that same quantity, '100%*$MMS'. Two things have to go right: read a threshold the article never states as a number, and express it against $MMS rather than resolving it to euros. cross_instrument is real here — the MMA itself is fixed by a Government nutarimas that is NOT ingested (see the mms entry) — so a proposal that keeps the reference is correct while one that inlines 1038 is not. ROUTING: `derived`, not `unchanged`. pipeline._derived_refs short-circuits any parameter whose stored value carries a $-reference straight to Routing.DERIVED, before retrieval and before any LLM call — "a value like `$PSS * 4` has no independent legislative existence: the anchor parameter is what legislation sets, so asking the corpus about the derived one is a guaranteed not_found". The first run of this case expected `unchanged` and scored it a model failure; the model was right and the ground truth was wrong. `expected_value` is therefore null (the value leg is not scored): what this case tests is that the pipeline recognises the formula and routes to the anchor instead of hunting the corpus for a number that is not in it. It keeps difficulty `derive` because the rung describes the parameter, not which legs score. | drafting warning: value leg not scored (no expected_value in the selection)
